old: Its name literally means 'without work' — a nod to a job it never does.
The Greek root means 'idle' or 'lazy,' describing a gas that reacts with nothing.
It shares its ending with 'carbon,' the word that set the pattern for naming noble gases.
clues: This chemical element was named after an ancient Greek word for 'idle' or 'lazy,' because it refuses to react with anything else.
A colorless noble gas making up about one percent of air, far more than helium or neon. It fills old-style light bulbs and shields welding from oxygen.
Element 18, it fills many double-pane windows for insulation. Its name's ending was borrowed from carbon, like those of its noble gas siblings neon and krypton.
